full_judgment:
S. K. Sinha J.:- This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 19th July, 2009 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 174 of 2008 discharging the Rule arising out of an application under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceedings in Sessions Case No. 1062 of 2006 arising out of C.R. Case No. 183 of 2006. 

 2. The respondent No. 2 filed the petition of complaint before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong being CR Case No. 183 of 2006 (Double mooring Zone) alleging, inter alia, that there was a regular business transaction between the accused-petitioner and the complainant. On 22nd November, 2005 and 23rd November, 2005, the accused petitioner paid 3(three) post dated cheques to the complainant amounting to Tk. 13,81,700/, The cheques were deposited with the United Commercial Bank for encashment but the said cheques were dishonored due to insufficient fund on 18th May, 2006. Thereafter on 23rd May, 2006 a legal notice was issued on behalf of the complainant upon the petitioner but the said notice was returned back with an endorsement that the recipient was not available. The complainant thereupon filed the petition of complainant. 

 4. On 8th October, 2006 the case record was transmitted to the Court of Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong for trial which was registered as Sessions Case No. 1062 of 2006. The learned Sessions Judge took cognizance of the case against the petitioner and fixed for appearance of the accused petitioner on 13th November, 2006. 

 5. On 15th August, 2006 charge was framed under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act against the accused-petitioner, to which; he pleaded not guilty and claimed as innocent. On 4th November, 2006, the case was fixed for trial. Thereafter the accused petitioner moved the High Court Division a petition under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for abashment of the proceedings. A Division Bench of the High Court Division after hearing discharged the rule. In this backdrop, the accused petitioner filed this criminal petition for leave to appeal.
